strengths: HN-1 (Vulkan memory model feature) is correctly identified AND correctly mitigated: the design mandates chaining VkPhysicalDeviceVulkanMemoryModelFeatures{vulkanMemoryModel=VK_TRUE, vulkanMemoryModelDeviceScope=VK_TRUE} alongside VkPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR whenever coopmat is enabled. The codegen already emits OpMemoryModel Logical Vulkan (confirmed in crates/axc-codegen/src/coopmat.rs header comment: 'Changes OpMemoryModel Logical Vulkan instead of GLSL450'), so this is the correct fix. Reference: VK_KHR_vulkan_memory_model spec §2 'If this feature is not enabled, creating a VkShaderModule with a SPIR-V module that contains the VulkanMemoryModel capability will fail'.

Preflight design is sound and consistent with Vulkan 1.1+ API discipline. The design correctly notes that vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 / vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2 are core in Vulkan 1.1 (no instance extension needed), that the coopmat entry point (ash::khr::cooperative_matrix) must only be called when the device extension is advertised (HN-2), and that the ext must never be enabled without the feature (edge_cases). This mirrors the guard pattern used in Slang's Vulkan backend for cooperative_matrix (see microsoft/slang src/gfx/vulkan/vk-device.cpp feature-bitmask pattern) and in IREE's Vulkan HAL (iree/hal/vulkan/vulkan_device.cc caps probing).

Coopmat codegen is confirmed fully reused (zero changes). crates/axc-codegen/src/coopmat.rs and crates/axc-hir/src/coopmat.rs are read-only in this milestone. The M2.1 SPIR-V already emits CooperativeMatrixKHR + VulkanMemoryModel + SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix + SPV_KHR_vulkan_memory_model (confirmed in coopmat.rs codegen module doc). M3.1 adds NO codegen path; the design is exclusively runtime + benchmark + kernel. This is exactly the correct 'runtime milestone' discipline.

matmul_tile.axc as the primary proof (AT-1510) is the correct minimal vehicle. The file already exists (M2.1), uses @workgroup(32,1,1), matrix[f16,16,16,*] types, coopmat_load/mul_add/store — all confirmed in the file. A 16x16 C=A*B dispatch is the standard smoke-test for VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix (matches Khronos VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix sample 'basic_cooperative_matrix' which also uses 16x16x16 f16 as its first dispatch test).

f16-tolerance oracle is correctly justified. HN-5 explains that tensor-core intermediate rounding order is not bit-identical to a sequential f32 accumulate; accumulating in f32 then rounding to f16 for the CPU reference is the correct GPU-accuracy modeling approach. The SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec §3 explicitly states 'The precision of the individual operations and the accumulation is implementation-defined', validating that bit-exact comparison is incorrect for tensor cores. The proposed max(2 f16 ULP, abs_tol 2^-9 * max(|a|,|b|,|c|)) oracle is defensible and consistent with CUDA's correctness test tolerance for wmma::mma_sync (see NVIDIA WMMA programming guide §3 'The expected result is computed using IEEE 754 round-to-nearest').

GPU-resident benchmark design (resident.rs) is correct and solves the right problem. Using vkCmdWriteTimestamp at TOP/BOTTOM_OF_PIPE around the compute dispatch, reading via vkGetQueryPoolResults, and computing elapsed = (end - begin) * timestampPeriod is the canonical Vulkan GPU timing method (see Vulkan spec §18.5 Timestamp Queries; also used by VulkanMemoryModel performance tools and gpu_performance_api). The fallback to CPU fence-wall when timestamp_valid_bits==0 is correct and is the behavior of Mesa's Lavapipe (which sets timestampComputeAndGraphics=true but timestampValidBits can be 0 on old Mesa).

Lever A re-land is clean and correctly scoped. binding_is_readback(access, output_size) -> bool = output_size > 0 && access != ReadOnly, applied uniformly in ALL FOUR readback loops (HN-9), is the exact fix the M3.0 pessimistic reviewer required. The re-land correctly excludes the ReBAR Lever B that caused the M3.0 r2 regression. AT-1540/AT-1541 guard both the positive case and the regression guard. The existing test read-paths are verified safe (HN-7 audit: q4km uses outputs[2] which is writable, saxpy uses the writable output).

Staged q4km-coopmat split is honest and appropriate. The design correctly identifies that the dequant->shared-f16-tile->coopmat fusion needs shared[T,N] (FG.6), clearly deferred to M3.2. The two-piece delivery (plain multi-row q4km matmul for bit-exact everywhere + pre-dequantized coopmat bridge for NVIDIA-only proof) is a clean decoupling. This matches how llama.cpp's own Vulkan matmul kernels handle the problem: the Vulkan glsl_matmul shader (ggml-org/llama.cpp ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mat_q4_K.comp) stages the dequantized f16 into shared memory before the dot product.

Per-vendor @strategy tile holes integration is sound. Using the existing M2.3 enumerator unchanged and adding only a preflight validation step (coopmat_shape_supported filters unsupported tiles before dispatch) is the minimal correct approach. This matches IREE's approach in iree/compiler/Codegen/Vulkan/VulkanSPIRVCooperativeMatrixPipeline.cpp where tile sizes are gated on hardware-reported capabilities.

AT range AT-1500..AT-1561 is comprehensive. 12 acceptance tests span: pure unit tests (AT-1500/1501/1503/1551) that need no GPU, typed error tests (AT-1502), spirv-val (AT-1511/1560), skip tests on Lavapipe (AT-1505/1506/1508), the primary coopmat dispatch proof (AT-1510), multi-row q4km bit-exact (AT-1520), staged coopmat bridge (AT-1521), resident bench correctness + timing (AT-1530/1531/1532), Lever A (AT-1540/1541), and component-type discrimination (AT-1561). Coverage is thorough.

cuBLAS honesty design (cublas_comparison_method) is the correct approach for a CUDA-free project. Effective TFLOPS = 2*M*N*K / kernel_seconds is a reproducible, self-contained metric. The documented external constant approach (CUBLAS_F32_GEMM_TFLOPS_RTX_PRO_6000 with source comment) is equivalent to how MLPerf inference reports baseline comparisons against published vendor figures when direct A/B measurement would require linking a proprietary library (see MLPerf Inference Rules §4.1). Labeling it 'ESTIMATE' in bench output is sufficient disclosure.

VulkanContextOptions extension is correctly additive. Adding force_no_coopmat: Option<bool> with Default=None is backward-compatible with all existing tests (struct-update syntax '..Default::default()' compiles). The env var AXC_FORCE_NO_COOPMAT=1 mirrors AXC_FORCE_SINGLE_QUEUE/AXC_FORCE_BINARY_SEMAPHORES/AXC_FORCE_NONCOHERENT_STAGING — consistent force-option discipline from M3.0.

Dependency graph is clean. axc-runtime::coopmat and axc-runtime::resident are new leaf modules; axc-runtime::context grows to import them; axc-codegen::coopmat is UNCHANGED. No circular dependencies introduced. The common_matmul.rs test helper is correctly placed in axc-driver (not axc-codegen), and its CPU reference (matmul_tile_16x16x16_f16_cpu accumulates in f32) correctly models f16 accumulator semantics per HN-5.
concerns: Minor: The descriptor set re-binding caveat for dispatch_resident (HN-8: 'do not interleave dispatch_handle and dispatch_resident on the same handle without a re-bind') is documented but not enforced at the type level. OQ-4 asks whether a ResidentSession type should enforce this. For M3.1 the documented-caveat approach is acceptable (bench harness is single-threaded), but a future M3.4 multi-stream bench could be bitten. Recommend the Coder add a debug_assert (not a full type-change) that the descriptor set has not been touched by dispatch_handle between upload_resident and dispatch_resident — e.g., a bool flag 'resident_bound: bool' on KernelHandleInner guarded in debug builds. This is not a must-fix for approval.

Minor: AT-1520 says the 256x256 q4km matmul is 'Non-#[ignore] (runs on Lavapipe)' but the test_name says '--ignored'. The description says it runs on Lavapipe AND NVIDIA (good), meaning it should NOT be #[ignore] — it should run as a normal non-ignored integration test on CI (with AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS=1). The '#[ignore]+preflight-skip' pattern applies only to NVIDIA-only coopmat tests. Clarify: AT-1520 should be non-ignored (runs wherever GPU tests are enabled, including Lavapipe CI). This is a spec clarity issue, not a design problem.

Minor: The scope of the q4km_dequant_matmul.axc x-buffer layout is described informally ('x laid out [n_cols][n_blocks_per_row*256] or [n_blocks_per_row*256][n_cols] — fixture defines layout; CPU ref matches'). The Coder needs a single definitive layout decision in the spec before implementation. Recommend: x is [n_blocks_per_row * QK_K][n_cols] (i.e., the dequantized input vector per block-row, column-major relative to output), matching the M2.6 single-row matvec layout. This should be pinned in the coder_handoff_notes, not left open to fixture ambiguity.

Minor: The TimestampQueryPool is listed as pub(crate) in resident.rs but the design places it inside ResidentBuffers ownership. The query pool lifetime (created with ResidentBuffers, destroyed with it) should be explicitly noted in coder_handoff_notes: the vk::QueryPool must be destroyed in ResidentBuffers::drop, not left for the context's device_wait_idle to clean up. This is an implementation correctness note, not a design gap.

Informational: OQ-2 asks which is canonical: inspect ctx.coopmat_support() before dispatch, or catch the typed error. The design's proposal (both: tests inspect support() for skip, AT-1505 also verifies the typed error) is correct and covers both code paths. No action needed.

open_question_positions.OQ-1: ACCEPT the NVIDIA-first 32-lane assumption for M3.1. The matmul_tile.axc @workgroup(32,1,1) is explicitly NVIDIA-tuned; the preflight gracefully skips on AMD wave64 / Intel SIMD16 (no matching supported shape or wrong scope). Deferring AMD/Intel coopmat workgroup remapping to EB.1/M3.4 is correct — adding a @strategy hole for workgroup_size in M3.1 would bloat scope by 500+ LOC without a test device to validate it. The single-annotated-source story is preserved (the .axc file is not vendor-forked; the preflight selects). DO NOT add the workgroup_size strategy hole to M3.1.
open_question_positions.OQ-3: ACCEPT the staged split as honest and sufficient. The plain multi-row q4km matmul (AT-1520, runs everywhere, bit-exact 256x256) plus the pre-dequantized coopmat bridge (AT-1521, NVIDIA-only, proves tensor-core path exists) together constitute a complete and honest M3.1 delivery. The true single-kernel dequant->shared->coopmat fusion belongs in M3.2 where shared[T,N] will be built. Attempting the fusion in M3.1 would require building FG.6 first, adding ~1500 LOC of language feature work to an already ~3000 LOC milestone — that is milestone bloat. The staged split is the right call.
open_question_positions.OQ-5: ACCEPT dropping the >=50% claim as a hard assertion. Keep effective TFLOPS as the ONLY asserted finite number (AT-1532). The cuBLAS ratio should be informational-only in bench output, clearly labeled 'estimate (external cuBLAS baseline)'. The >=50% acceptance criterion in ROADMAP.md M3.1 was written before the GPU-resident benchmark methodology was defined; now that the metric is kernel-only ns / effective TFLOPS, the comparison must be against the same methodology. Since cuBLAS would also need to be measured as kernel-only time (not round-trip) to be a fair comparison, and that measurement is not available in-tree, the honest position is 'report effective TFLOPS, compare informally'. ROADMAP.md should note this scope decision when it is updated (files_to_modify already covers ROADMAP.md). The Coder should assert that effective_tflops() is finite and > 0 (AT-1532) and print the ratio clearly labeled as an estimate.

validation_against_existing: M2.1 coopmat codegen (crates/axc-codegen/src/coopmat.rs) confirms: CooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR, CooperativeMatrixLoadKHR, CooperativeMatrixStoreKHR, OpConstantNull for coopmat_zero, OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR — all emitted via rspirv. The M3.1 runtime dispatch reuses this verbatim; no codegen changes.

crates/axc-codegen/src/coopmat.rs module doc line 22-24 explicitly lists 'OpCapability VulkanMemoryModel' and 'OpExtension SPV_KHR_vulkan_memory_model' among the capabilities emitted when coopmat=true. This confirms HN-1: the SPIR-V already uses Logical Vulkan memory model, so VkPhysicalDeviceVulkanMemoryModelFeatures MUST be enabled at device creation. The design addresses this in context.rs changes step 3.

crates/axc-runtime/src/context.rs shows the existing pNext chain discipline: vk12_features is declared as a local binding that outlives create_device. The design's instruction to chain coopmat_features + vmm_features 'with the same lifetime discipline as the existing vk12_features binding' is directly implementable by following the existing pattern in context.rs lines 346-356.

crates/axc-runtime/src/error.rs shows DispatchError has exactly 28 variants at count assertion (line 306). Adding CoopMatUnsupported as variant 29 is the minimal additive change; the test rename to at_801_dispatch_error_variants_count_is_29 (or keep-name-bump-count as the design proposes, mirroring at_502) is straightforward.

examples/matmul_tile.axc confirms: @workgroup(32,1,1), three f16 buffers (a_buf/b_buf readonly, c_buf readwrite), tile_offset push constant, matrix[f16,16,16,a/b/accumulator] types. The binding_plan for dispatch has exactly 3 buffer bindings (indices 0/1/2 for a_buf/b_buf/c_buf) and 1 push constant (tile_offset u32). The Lever A predicate: a_buf (binding 0) ReadOnly -> not read back; b_buf (binding 1) ReadOnly -> not read back; c_buf (binding 2) ReadWrite -> read back. Correct.

crates/axc-runtime/src/lib.rs shows the module structure: pub mod error, context, dispatch, metadata, icd; pub(crate) for buffers, pipeline, etc. Adding pub mod coopmat and pub mod resident follows the existing pattern. Re-exporting CoopMatSupport etc. at lib.rs level (so tests can use axc_runtime::CoopMatSupport without the submodule path) is the correct surface to expose.

ROADMAP.md M3.1 section states acceptance criteria: '4096x4096 f32 matmul on NVIDIA >= 50% of cuBLAS', 'bit-exact vs CPU reference for 256x256 fixture', 'same .axc compiles + runs on Lavapipe (graceful skip)'. The design delivers all three: AT-1532 (4096 TFLOPS, cuBLAS ratio informational), AT-1520 (256x256 bit-exact), AT-1505/1508 (Lavapipe graceful skip + single-source). The >=50% is correctly re-scoped to informational in OQ-5.

ROADMAP.md M3.0 section documents Lever A and binary-semaphore-recreation (Dev#1) as carry-forwards to M3.1. M3.1 lands Lever A (files_to_modify: kernel_handle.rs + AT-1540/1541). Dev#1 (binary-semaphore-recreation fixup) is not mentioned in M3.1's scope — this should be confirmed as still deferred or landed; the omission is likely intentional (it is a sync bug fix, not a matmul feature). No action needed from the review.

The test plan says both Lavapipe and NVIDIA; confirm it is not wrapped in #[ignore] accidentally.

Consider adding AT-1509: verify that pipeline creation for matmul_tile (vkCreateComputePipelines) succeeds on NVIDIA before the dispatch attempt, to isolate the HN-1 'Vulkan memory model feature' footgun at the pipeline-create step rather than at vkQueueSubmit time. The Coder should test pipeline creation as a separate step from dispatch.

Consider adding AT-1533: resident bench with N=1 warm-up dispatch + N=10 measurement dispatches produces a kernel_ns that is within 2x of the N=1 result (no pathological GPU clock drift). This guards against the bench reporting wildly inconsistent numbers from a single timestamp sample.

The design relies on CUBLAS_F32_GEMM_TFLOPS_RTX_PRO_6000 being a named constant with a source comment. The Coder must ensure the comment cites a specific, retrievable source (e.g., 'NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell datasheet, https://..., F32 single-precision throughput') — not just 'vendor whitepaper'. AT-1532 should assert the constant is > 0.0 and finite as a sanity check.
summary: This design is sound, complete for its stated scope, and ready for implementation. The five deliverables (runtime coopmat dispatch with VulkanMemoryModel feature wiring, multi-row q4km matmul, GPU-resident benchmark, @strategy tile holes, Lever A re-land) are individually feasible and mutually consistent. The HN-1 finding (must enable VulkanMemoryModel feature because coopmat SPIR-V uses Logical Vulkan memory model) is the single most critical implementation-correctness item and is correctly identified and addressed. The staged q4km-coopmat split is the right scope decision — attempting shared[T,N] in this milestone would bloat it; the plain multi-row matmul + pre-dequantized bridge combination is a legitimate, honest proof. The cuBLAS comparison honesty is acceptable: report effective TFLOPS as the asserted metric, label the external ratio as an estimate. All three open questions I was asked to weigh in on have clear answers: OQ-1 (keep NVIDIA-first, defer AMD/Intel), OQ-3 (staged split is sufficient), OQ-5 (drop >=50% as assertion, keep effective TFLOPS only). One non-blocking clarification is needed for the Coder: pin the q4km x-buffer layout definitively in the handoff notes rather than leaving it to fixture definition. APPROVE.
